text:
Ben Chiarot is 35, in his fifth season in Detroit, and playing more than ever: about 21 minutes a night over his last ten games, up a minute and a half on his season average, on a team that has lost six of those ten. He has 2 assists and no goals in 21 games.

Nobody keeps Chiarot around for points, so the question is what the minutes buy. Our numbers aren't kind. At five on five the Red Wings have 48.7% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on, slightly worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey was blunter about last season: around replacement level, with opponents getting more chances with him out there than against almost any other defenseman (bottom 1%). His plays-like matches share the same flag, chances against piling up.

In fairness, he's been a little unlucky this year (results about three goals worse than the chances), and he blocks shots (30) and throws hits. But a 35-year-old soaking up top-four minutes on a struggling team is a sign of how thin the blue line is, not a solution to it.
